item.text: The implementation now migrates existing databases to `priority='Normal'`, returns saved priority with tasks, and accepts only the three specified priority values. I’m checking startup, the health endpoint, priority persistence across a restart, and that task state remains intact.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc 'tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
export DB_PATH="$tmpdir/workboard.sqlite" PORT=18080
npm start >"$tmpdir/server.log" 2>&1 &
pid=$!
cleanup() { kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT
for attempt in $(seq 1 30); do
  if curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:18080/health >"$tmpdir/health.json"; then break; fi
  sleep 0.2
done
cat "$tmpdir/health.json"
curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18080/api/projects -H '"'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"name\":\"Pilot\"}' >\""'$tmpdir/project.json"
project_id=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(require('"'fs').readFileSync(process.argv[1])).id)\" \""'$tmpdir/project.json")
curl -fsS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:18080/api/projects/$project_id/tasks" -H '"'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"title\":\"Check priority\"}' >\""'$tmpdir/task.json"
task_id=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.parse(require('"'fs').readFileSync(process.argv[1])).id)\" \""'$tmpdir/task.json")
curl -fsS -X PATCH "http://127.0.0.1:18080/api/projects/$project_id/tasks/$task_id" -H '"'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"priority\":\"High\"}'
cleanup
trap - EXIT
npm start >\""'$tmpdir/server-restart.log" 2>&1 &
pid=$!
trap cleanup EXIT
for attempt in $(seq 1 30); do
  if curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:18080/api/projects/$project_id/tasks" >"$tmpdir/tasks.json"; then break; fi
  sleep 0.2
done
node -e "const tasks=JSON.parse(require('"'fs').readFileSync(process.argv[1])); if(tasks.length"'!==1||tasks[0].priority!=='"'High'||tasks[0].title"'!=='"'Check priority') process.exit(1); console.log(JSON.stringify(tasks))\" \""'$tmpdir/tasks.json"
'

item.text:
Implemented task priorities and committed as `f3f5ffe4c78196a47ede4222b3cb27873df504eb`.

Each task now has a `Low`, `Normal`, or `High` selector. Priority defaults to `Normal`, persists in SQLite, and is disabled for archived projects. Existing databases are migrated automatically.

Verified JavaScript syntax, `git diff --check`, the health endpoint, and priority persistence across a server restart. The working tree is clean.

Run with `npm start`; the server uses `PORT` (default `8080`) and `DB_PATH` for SQLite storage.
